problem: Recent claims (FGPrompt, OVRL-v2) say image-goal navigation can be learned end-to-end with RL alone using small CNNs, while DEBiT needs relative-pose pre-training. Evaluation protocols differ across papers, and the role of architecture and simulator settings is unclear.
motivation: If RL alone could train image comparison, relative pose estimation could be learned from navigation reward with no pose labels. The authors train all agents under identical conditions and vary architecture (late fusion, channel stacking, space-to-depth, cross-attention) and the Habitat sliding flag to test this.
key_idea: Under identical training, show that the apparent success of RL-only channel-stacking agents comes mostly from Habitat's Sliding=True setting, and that early patch-wise fusion with pre-training is what really works.
insight: With Sliding=True, ChannelCat ResNet9 reaches 83.2 SR, but with Sliding=False it drops to 44.6 (ResNet9+s2d: 83.6 to 31.7), while pre-trained DEBiT holds at 81.7. The easier sliding setting lets the perception module get trained, and those weights transfer: loading perception weights alone gives 38.5 SR versus 31.7 from scratch, and loading the full agent and fine-tuning gives 65.7. Probing shows navigation SR correlates with emergent relative-pose accuracy, and late fusion, even with pre-trained encoders, stays poor (DEBiT-ViT 38.6 vs 96.8 at 2m/20°).
method: Base agent: a recurrent GRU policy (2 layers, hidden 128) with a binocular encoder φ(o_t,g), a previous-action embedding and a linear actor-critic, trained from scratch with PPO. Reward is 10·success − Δgeodesic − 0.01.

Encoder variants: Late Fusion (two separate encoders, concatenated embeddings), ChannelCat (6-channel stacked input), SpaceToDepth (FGPrompt/ZSEL ResNet9), ViT-Small, and DEBiT-B cross-attention (frozen pre-trained on relative pose and visibility estimation, plus a ResNet18 observation encoder, or trained from scratch).
Sliding ablation: train and evaluate every agent with Habitat Sliding=True or False; an audit of code repositories found FGPrompt uses the default True while the others set False.
Transfer experiments: load or freeze or fine-tune the perception part (φ) and/or the action part (GRU, ζ, π) of a Sliding=True agent into the Sliding=False setting, for ChannelCat+s2d and DEBiT.

RPVE probing: freeze φ and train a ~3M-parameter head to predict relative translation, rotation and visibility on ~68M image pairs from Gibson, MP3D and HM3D, then correlate probe accuracy with navigation SR.
Failure analysis: Sankey plots of success, timeout and early-stop over 994 episodes across models.

setting.backbone: ResNet9 / ViT-Small (trained from scratch with RL) and DEBiT-B (frozen RPVE-pretrained binocular ViT + ResNet18), all with a GRU policy
setting.model_size: ResNet9 (small); ViT-Small; DEBiT-B; GRU 2x128; probe head ~3M
setting.training_data: Gibson 72 train scenes, 500M PPO steps per agent; DEBiT encoder pre-trained on CroCo and RPVE (from prior work); probing set ~68M pairs from Gibson/MP3D/HM3D
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 112x112 plus goal image (no depth, no GPS/compass)
setting.action_space: low-level: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT 10°, TURN RIGHT 10°, STOP

numbers.extra: encoder pre-trained on RPVE; 1000 step budget; success radius 1 m; realistic Sliding=False

numbers.method: ChannelCat+s2d trained Sliding=True, then fine-tuned 100M steps on Sliding=False
numbers.extra: transfer: full agent loaded from Sliding=True and fine-tuned; evaluated Sliding=False

numbers_note: Values are on the Gibson val split (14 scenes) with the standard Habitat ImageNav episodes.
results: With Sliding=True, RL-only ChannelCat ResNet9 reaches 83.2-83.6 SR, close to pre-trained DEBiT (90.5). With Sliding=False, ChannelCat drops to 31.7-44.6 SR while DEBiT stays at 81.7. Cross-attention without pre-training scores 0 SR, and late fusion stays at about 7-14 SR.
limitations: Only Gibson ImageNav in Habitat with RGB-only agents; no real-robot tests.
The explanation of undertraining under Sliding=False is a conjecture, only supported indirectly by transfer and probing results.
Probing correlation rests on few models, and the pre-trained DEBiT probing numbers are not comparable.
